newsitem.title: USA: General Instrument expects weak earnings.
newsitem.headline: General Instrument expects weak earnings.

text.p: General Instrument Corp, which earlier reported a third-quarter profit versus a loss, said Wednesday it expects per share earnings for the fourth quarter and for 1997 to be below expectations.

For the fourth quarter, General Instrument said earnings are expected to be in a range of $0.28 to $0.32 per fully diluted share. Earning on a fully diluted per-share basis in 1997 are expected to be 25 to 35 percent above 1996 levels.
Order weakness at Power Semiconductor will result in lower sales and earnings growth in the coming quarters, it said. Lower demand for consumer satellite products will hurt fourth-quarter results.
In 1997, increased investment will be required to fund the successful deployment and market growth of telephony networks at Next Level Communications, the company added.

"These near-term factors do not alter the fundamental strength of General Instrument's market position," said Richard Friedland, chairman and chief executive "In those parts of our business that are temporarily experiencing weak demand, we have taken action to reduce operating expenses and defer capital spending until growth trends resume."

Earlier, General Instrument said it earned $42.1 million, or $0.30 per fully diluted share, in the third quarter versus a loss of $40.9 million, or $0.33 diluted share, in the same period in 1995. Last year's results include a $90 million after-tax charge for an acquisition and technology write-off.
